scoring_justification: The agent's reported nucleation rate and supersaturation are compared to the paper's theoretical values with generous tolerances (factor 10 for J, ±50% for S). Although the full flow and solubility models cannot be rerun in the checker, this T0 comparison is feasible because the paper provides exact numbers as hidden gold, and the tolerances accommodate implementation spread.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-reported nucleation rates and supersaturation at capillary exit for CO2/benzoic acid and CHF3/benzoic acid, and ordering among the three systems.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text (Section 3): 'S equals approximately 3 at the capillary exit in case of CHF3/benzoic acid and approximately 31 in case of CO2/benzoic acid. The corresponding nucleation rates are 6×10^16 and about 10^26 cm^-3 s^-1' and the statement that CO2/benzoic acid > CO2/cholesterol > CHF3/benzoic acid.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Exact values as written; tolerances set per approved verification strategy: order-of-magnitude (factor 10) for J, ±50% relative for S, wide threshold for CO2/cholesterol J (1e15–1e24), and required ordering of J among the three systems.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's own reported theoretical results, not arbitrary numbers.

outputs.description: Nucleation rate J (cm⁻³ s⁻¹) and supersaturation S (dimensionless) at the capillary exit for the three solute–solvent systems under the reference pre-expansion and nozzle conditions. The hidden checker compares these values against the paper's theoretical results using generous tolerances appropriate for re‑implementation differences.

output_contract.notes: The experimental particle size measurements are excluded. The reference conditions and all material parameters required for the computation are stated in the instruction. The checker uses tolerances that absorb numerical implementation spread while still requiring genuine re‑execution of the workflow.
